queue.title: My neighbor tried to sue me over a fence I built. They didn't realize I'm a professional surveyor and they've been living on 2 feet of my land for a decade.
queue.body: So my neighbor (let's call him Dave) has always been a pain. Last week he served me papers claiming my new fence was 6 inches onto his property. Dave didn't realize that I'm actually a professional land surveyor. I went out, pulled the original pins, and confirmed the property line. Turns out, his entire driveway and 2 feet of his yard are actually on MY property. When I showed him the survey, his lawyer immediately dropped the case. I'm now considering building a new, much larger fence right on the actual line, which would cut his driveway in half. Petty? Maybe. Satisfying? Absolutely.
queue.author: SurveyorJustice

queue.title: TIFU by explaining exactly how a specific lock works to a group of friends, only to realize I'd just shown them how to break into my own apartment.
queue.body: I'm a bit of a lockpicking enthusiast and I've spent hundreds of hours learning how different security systems work. Last night I was hanging out with some friends and we got on the topic of home security. I decided to show off a bit and explained the exact vulnerability of the 'unpickable' lock I have on my front door. I went into detail about the specific tensioning technique and the blind spot in the cylinder. About halfway through, I saw my friends' faces and realized I'd just given four people a step-by-step guide on how to get into my apartment in under 30 seconds. Now I'm sitting here ordering a completely different lock system and feeling like an absolute idiot. TIFU by being an expert at my own expense.
queue.author: SecurityFlaw
